title: Unlocking the Future of Physical & Virtual Security: Securex 2026
description: Attending Day 1 of Securex South Africa 2026 at the Gallagher Convention Centre was an incredible experience that completely shifted my perspective on where software meets physical infrastructure. Walking the exhibition floors made one macro-trend visibly obvious - the modern security market is entirely focused on maximizing what physical hardware can achieve by supercharging it with intelligent software layer integrations.

From autonomous drone grids managed by 24:7 Drone Force to smart perimeter systems by ClearVu and Nemtek, the gap between physical installation and full-stack software development has completely vanished. Witnessing how 24:7 Drone Force deploys remote monitoring systems and drone fleets was a standout highlight, by using software to gain real-time tactical insights on the ground, they effectively remove human operators and drone fighters from immediate danger in the wild. Nearby, industry giants like Hikvision, Suprema, and Eagle Eye Networks showcased an ecosystem driven by AI, smart cameras, lock pads, and biometric fingerprint sensors completely unified for asynchronous authentication, automated logging, and granular access control.

As a developer with hands-on experience configuring security groups, access control, and VMS networks, these systems felt incredibly familiar yet deeply progressive. The key takeaway here is that the modern security objective isn't just to build isolated software solutions, but to engineer highly functional, deeply integratable systems that plug seamlessly into existing infrastructures. In an industry where lives and enterprise assets are on the line, operational reliability and absolute consistency are the foundational keys.

This expo highlighted exactly how we can leverage modern DevOps and full-stack engineering within physical security frameworks. By containerizing lightweight microservices at the network layer or even on resource hardware. We can build smart middleware applications that parse telemetry data, secure IoT endpoints, and automate monitoring workflows. The future belongs to developers who build highly resilient, integratable systems bridging the physical and digital worlds, and I’m excited to weave these architecture principles into my upcoming software builds.

title: What the Industry Has Shown Me - Halfway Through My Internship Journey
description: This month marks the halfway point of my 6-month internship with the Department of Correctional Services, and the experience has been eye-opening in ways I didn’t expect.

One of the biggest lessons I’ve learned is that you’re never a one-man team. Asking for help isn’t weakness-it's collaboration. I’ve also realized that no one will hand you everything on a silver platter; to grow, you need to be curious, proactive, and driven to learn.

Working in such a sensitive environment has shown me the powerful role the Department plays-not only in ensuring security, but also in rehabilitation. Rehabilitation goes beyond physical systems; it includes mental and spiritual well-being. Just this week, I attended a service hosted by the Spiritual Care Department that focused on strengthening mental health and spiritual growth, a reminder of the holistic approach the Department takes.

On the technical side, my learning has been just as rich: strengthening social and communication skills while working in diverse teams, gaining hands-on exposure to security groups and large-scale network configurations, adapting to internal systems unique to the Department, and recognizing the impact of my work on something larger than myself.

title: AWS Summit Johannesburg 2024
description: Thank you to Amazon Web Services (AWS) for hosting us at their Summit. While the event exceeded expectations in some areas, I found the overall experience to be a mix of familiar and novel elements.

I particularly appreciated the inclusive nature of the Summit, offering something for everyone. One highlight was attending Mohammed Zaakir Ally's session at the AWSome Theater, where he discussed TriState Capital Bank's integration with PayShap SA's real-time money transfer technology-no account numbers needed. His in-person demo, which he showed me during our chat, was impressive and sparked my interest in their innovative approach.

I also enjoyed the ML/AI presentation and was impressed by AWS's commitment to using their own infrastructure to develop new protocols like Nitro. Their re-imagining of hypervisors, hardware, and security demonstrates dedication to cutting-edge solutions.

I wish I'd networked more with participants-something I'll prioritize at the next one. Special thanks to Amogelang Chaane, Ororiseng Mabaso, Letlotlo Leballo, and Qualtrix Software Technologies for their support.

title: Motsepe Foundation Youth Tech Expo 2024
description: Kicked off the weekend on a positive note! It was a stimulating experience to engage with insightful thought leaders at the Motsepe Foundation hashtag#youthtechexpo . I particularly appreciate their initiative to empower the youth, give as much information as possible and opportunities to talk to drivers. Inspired by my passion for knowledge sharing, I conducted interviews at several booths. Unfortunately, the information on my SD card became corrupted, but I'm happy to share my key takeaways below:

Focuses on equipping interns with the right mindset and professional behaviors for workplace success. I particularly loved their book, it also has a centralized portal for accessing school resources, bursary opportunities, and internship placements.

Harambee Youth Employment Accelerator a key partner in the sayouth.mobi platform.This platform provides a field-agnostic opportunity for young people to access free learning and earning opportunities through a data-free mobile site.Sa Youth collaborates with various stakeholders including government institutions, NGOs, businesses, and entrepreneurs to connect youth with these opportunities. What I loved about it, it was none field specific.

A tech community for all - youth, skilled, ambitious etc. Though not my first time seeing/interacting with the organisation this time I had the opportunity to speak with one it's co-founder Mixo Ngoveni and he spoke about his journey from pushing to just getting a booth at the event to now being one of the speakers. He had this energy that kept reminding me of his drive to accomplish goals and help others without it feeling forced. This is a go to community I always recommend for new and already established people in tech.
